note: a refresh driven by the change feed (STORAGE.md section 4.5, SEARCH.md section 4): each case builds its store as store.json's are built and indexes it, then applies its steps in order, each as an owner would write it. After each step the feed lists, above the cursor read before it, the items and the collections stated in changed, and the purge count moves when purged says so; a refresh then answers each query as stated, as an index rebuilt from the store as it then stands does, but in a step stating lagging, which answers its queries before the refresh. A missing stamp leaves the index answering the earlier store.

cases.label: every kind of write an owner makes

steps.note: an insert takes the next stamp
a flag added to a placement, the body unchanged
a body replaced under the same link id
a summary row changed under an unchanged item: its object, flags, level and sort key stay, so no trigger draws a stamp and the writer requests one (stamp_item)
a source's coverage moving restamps its collection and none of its items
a rename restamps every item under the new id and counts as a purge, the old keys gone
an item every source dropped is retained: stamped, and no longer searched
a purged item cannot carry a stamp and counts as a purge
the card dropped, then erased (STORAGE section 11.5): its purge and the collected body count as purges

cases.label: a body goes with its last placement
cases.note: the card's first body is replaced, then the card retained: each body leaves the index with the last placement naming it, though the store still holds it, uncollected or pinned by the retained row, as an index rebuilt then would hold it (SEARCH.md section 4)

cases.label: a member whose sort key moves names and bounds its thread again
cases.note: basic-1 and follow-1, which replies to it, are one thread named after basic-1, the earlier. follow-1's date, and so its sort key, moves before basic-1's: the thread is named after follow-1 and bounded by the two dates as they stand, as an index rebuilt then would name and bound it (SEARCH.md section 9)

cases.label: an event in a zone whose rule steps by the second is indexed within bounds
cases.note: event-zoned-hostile.ics: its zone's DAYLIGHT rule steps every second from 1970, which an expander following every onset walks for 1.7 billion steps; STORAGE.md Annex A.3 and SEARCH.md section 7 bound the periods a rule is followed for, so indexing the event ends and it answers by the fields it states, its title and its kind; the instant a zone this hostile resolves to is the implementation's own and no query here reads it (SEARCH.md section 7)

cases.label: an item keeps local state
cases.note: properties (STORAGE section 4.3) are applied by the owner from set-property actions (section 15.3), keyed by the seq, read from the store by label: and property:, never copied into the index; a change stamps every row holding the seq, a change that moves no row stamps nothing

steps.note: a label added stamps every row holding the item's seq, in both accounts (STORAGE section 4.5)
a label whose fold the item holds already adds nothing and stamps nothing (STORAGE section 15.3), queued on the other collection
respelled: the remove takes the label whose fold is its own, then the add writes the new spelling
a value the item does not hold, removed, changes nothing
one row retained: its item keeps its properties, read from the live row alone
that row purged: another row holds the seq, so the properties stay
an application's own value removed

cases.label: a system flag is read from the store as it stands
cases.note: is: and a tag: naming a system flag read the store's items.marks when the query runs (SEARCH.md section 8.2), never the index, so a step stating lagging, answered before the refresh with the index one write behind, answers the flags the write left; a keyword is read from the index's flag table, once refreshed

steps.note: a message marked read and flagged in one of its two collections, answered before the refresh: no longer unread, since a placement holds the bit, and flagged
the reply marked unread, answered before the refresh
a keyword added, answered after the refresh: the keyword from the index, the system flags from the store, a text term beside them
the reply marked answered and draft, its \Seen dropped, answered before the refresh

cases.label: a hit holding two bodies holds a text term through either
cases.note: split-1 is filed in two collections of one account, one seq, the INBOX copy under a body saying quince and the Archive copy under one saying rhubarb, as two clients may file one Message-ID under bodies differing in a header. A text term holds for the hit when any of its placements matches it (SEARCH.md section 8.2), so quince rhubarb holds and quince not rhubarb does not, though no body holds both words: a count matching whole documents answers otherwise unless it evaluates the seq per placement. The steps file the Archive copy under the other body, repoint it to the INBOX body, back to its own, then remove it
